page: Amazon Web Services c7i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processors running at 3.2 GHz, delivering 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 384 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on external network storage and utilizing a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The Intel Xeon processors support advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which drive top-tier results in cryptography, ray tracing, and image processing. Memory read bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching top-tier status in both cached and uncached read tests, though write bandwidth and overall PassMark memory scores fall into the strong and average tiers respectively.

The c7i.metal-48xl offers high compute density and bare-metal access, eliminating virtualization overhead. This makes it highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that can fully exploit its 192 threads and specialized instruction sets like AMX. However, tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage, requiring reliance on network-attached storage, and a low memory-to-vCPU ratio that limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases.

This server is designed for high-performance computing (HPC), heavy multi-threaded compilation, cryptography, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference. It is particularly effective for large-model LLM prompt processing, where it achieves top-tier benchmark throughput.
